en.display_text:
**Consider the following statements:**

**Statement-I:**
The atmosphere is heated more by incoming solar radiation than by terrestrial radiation.

**Statement-II:**
Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere are good absorbers of long wave radiation.

**Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?**

(a) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I

(b) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I

(c) Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect

(d) Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct

statement_analysis.statement: The atmosphere is heated more by incoming solar radiation than by terrestrial radiation.
statement_analysis.reason: Atmosphere is primarily heated by terrestrial (longwave) radiation emitted from Earth's surface, not by direct incoming solar (shortwave) radiation.

statement_analysis.statement: Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere are good absorbers of long wave radiation.
statement_analysis.reason: Greenhouse gases like CO2 absorb longwave (infrared) radiation effectively, contributing to the greenhouse effect.

elimination_logic: Statement-I is factually incorrect, so options (a) and (b) are eliminated.
Statement-II is correct, so option (c) is eliminated.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in the common misconception that the atmosphere is mainly heated by direct solar radiation. UPSC tests understanding of the greenhouse effect and the distinction between shortwave and longwave radiation absorption.
en.final_explanation:
Option (d) is correct because **Statement-I is incorrect:** the atmosphere is not heated more by incoming solar radiation, but rather by terrestrial (longwave) radiation re-emitted from Earth's surface. 

**Statement-II is correct:** greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide are effective absorbers of longwave radiation, which is the basis of the greenhouse effect. This distinction is fundamental in climatology and atmospheric science. 

**The question tests the ability to differentiate between the sources of atmospheric heating and the role of greenhouse gases.**

वायुमंडल को पृथ्वी से आने वाली विकिरण (terrestrial radiation) की तुलना में सीधे आने वाली सौर विकिरण से अधिक गर्म किया जाता है।

वायुमंडल में मौजूद कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड और अन्य ग्रीनहाउस गैसें दीर्घतरंग विकिरण (long wave radiation) को अच्छी तरह अवशोषित करती हैं।

(c) कथन-I सही है, लेकिन कथन-II गलत है

(d) कथन-I गलत है, लेकिन कथन-II सही है

कथन-II सही है, इसलिए विकल्प (c) को हटा दिया गया।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: यह जाल इस सामान्य भ्रांति में है कि वायुमंडल मुख्यतः सीधे सौर विकिरण से गर्म होता है। UPSC ग्रीनहाउस प्रभाव और लघु तरंग तथा दीर्घतरंग विकिरण के अवशोषण के बीच अंतर को समझने की क्षमता का परीक्षण करता है।

**कथन-II सही है:** कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड जैसी ग्रीनहाउस गैसें दीर्घतरंग विकिरण को प्रभावी रूप से अवशोषित करती हैं, जो ग्रीनहाउस प्रभाव का आधार है। यह भेद जलवायु विज्ञान और वायुमंडलीय विज्ञान में मौलिक है। 

**यह प्रश्न वायुमंडलीय ताप के स्रोतों और ग्रीनहाउस गैसों की भूमिका के बीच अंतर करने की क्षमता का परीक्षण करता है।**

en.display_text:
**Consider the following statements:**

**Statement-I:**
Thickness of the troposphere at the equator is much greater as compared to poles.

**Statement-II:**
At the equator, heat is transported to great heights by strong convectional currents.

**Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?**

(a) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I.

(b) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.

(c) Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect.

(d) Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.

statement_analysis.statement: Thickness of the troposphere at the equator is much greater as compared to poles.
statement_analysis.reason: The troposphere is thickest at the equator (about 17-18 km) and thinnest at the poles (about 8-9 km) due to higher surface heating and convection.

statement_analysis.statement: At the equator, heat is transported to great heights by strong convectional currents.
statement_analysis.reason: Intense solar heating at the equator causes strong convection, lifting air to greater heights and increasing troposphere thickness.

elimination_logic: Options c and d are eliminated because both statements are correct.
Option b is eliminated because Statement-II directly explains Statement-I.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The main trap is causation-fallacy: candidates may believe both statements are true but miss that Statement-II is the direct reason for Statement-I. UPSC tests if aspirants can link cause (convection) and effect (troposphere thickness).
en.final_explanation:
**Option (a) is correct** because both statements are factually accurate and Statement-II provides the direct explanation for Statement-I. 

The troposphere is thickest at the equator due to intense solar heating, which causes strong convectional currents that lift air to greater heights. 

This process results in a thicker troposphere at the equator compared to the poles, where such convection is much weaker. 

**Understanding the link between surface heating, convection, and atmospheric structure is crucial for this question.**

en.display_text:
**Consider the following:**

1. Pyroclastic debris

2. Ash and dust

3. Nitrogen compounds

4. Sulphur compounds

**How many of the above are products of volcanic eruptions?**

(a) Only one

(b) Only two

(c) Only three

(d) All four

statement_analysis.statement: Pyroclastic debris
statement_analysis.reason: Pyroclastic debris is a classic product of explosive volcanic eruptions, consisting of rock fragments and volcanic material.

statement_analysis.statement: Ash and dust
statement_analysis.reason: Volcanic eruptions emit large quantities of ash and dust into the atmosphere.

statement_analysis.statement: Nitrogen compounds
statement_analysis.reason: Nitrogen compounds, though less prominent, can be released during volcanic eruptions due to high-temperature reactions.

statement_analysis.statement: Sulphur compounds
statement_analysis.reason: Sulphur compounds, especially sulphur dioxide, are major gaseous emissions from volcanoes.

elimination_logic: Pyroclastic debris, ash and dust, and sulphur compounds are universally recognized volcanic products, eliminating options a and b.
Nitrogen compounds, though less emphasized, are also released, eliminating option c.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in the inclusion of nitrogen compounds, which are less commonly discussed as volcanic products. Candidates may overlook this and select option c, missing the comprehensive nature of volcanic emissions.
en.final_explanation:
All four listed items—pyroclastic debris, ash and dust, nitrogen compounds, and sulphur compounds—are products of volcanic eruptions. 

While the first three are widely recognized, nitrogen compounds are also released due to high-temperature chemical reactions during eruptions. Volcanic activity emits a wide range of materials, including solid fragments, fine ash, and various gases such as sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. 

Therefore, the correct answer is option d, as all four are valid products of volcanic eruptions.

**Which of the following is/are correct inference/inferences from isothermal maps in the month of January?**

1. The isotherms deviate to the north over the ocean and to the south over the continent.

2. The presence of cold ocean currents, Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift make the North Atlantic Ocean colder and the isotherms bend towards the north.

**Select the answer using the code given below:
**
(a) 1 only

(b) 2 only

(c) Both 1 and 2

(d) Neither 1 nor 2

statement_analysis.statement: The isotherms deviate to the north over the ocean and to the south over the continent.
statement_analysis.reason: In January, isotherms bend northward over oceans (due to moderating effect) and southward over continents (due to greater cooling).

statement_analysis.statement: The presence of cold ocean currents, Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift make the North Atlantic Ocean colder and the isotherms bend towards the north.
statement_analysis.reason: Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift are warm currents, making the North Atlantic Ocean warmer, not colder; isotherms bend north due to this warming.

elimination_logic: Statement 2 is factually incorrect; eliminate options containing it.
Statement 1 is correct; eliminate options that exclude it.

en.display_text:
**Consider the following statements:**

**Statement-I:** 
Rainfall is one of the reasons for weathering of rocks.

**Statement-II:** 
Rainwater contains carbon dioxide in solution.

**Statement-III: **
Rainwater contains atmospheric oxygen.

**Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?**

(a) Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I.
(b) Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I.
(c) Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I.
(d) Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct.

statement_analysis.statement: Statement-I: Rainfall is one of the reasons for weathering of rocks.
statement_analysis.reason: Rainfall contributes to both physical and chemical weathering of rocks.

statement_analysis.statement: Statement-II: Rainwater contains carbon dioxide in solution.
statement_analysis.reason: Rainwater absorbs atmospheric CO2, forming weak carbonic acid, which aids chemical weathering.

statement_analysis.statement: Statement-III: Rainwater contains atmospheric oxygen.
statement_analysis.reason: Rainwater dissolves atmospheric oxygen, which participates in oxidation processes during weathering.

elimination_logic: Options c and d are eliminated as both II and III are correct.
Option b is eliminated because both II and III explain Statement-I, not just one.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in testing whether candidates know that both dissolved CO2 and O2 in rainwater contribute to weathering, and not just one. Many may think only CO2 is relevant, overlooking the role of oxygen in oxidation.
en.final_explanation:
**Option (a) is correct** because both carbon dioxide and oxygen dissolved in rainwater play significant roles in the weathering of rocks. Carbon dioxide forms weak carbonic acid with rainwater, leading to carbonation, while oxygen enables oxidation reactions. 

Both processes are central to chemical weathering. Thus, both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both explain how rainfall contributes to the weathering of rocks.

1. It increases with increase in wind velocity.

en.final_explanation:
**Option c is correct** because both statements accurately describe the Coriolis force. 

The Coriolis force, caused by Earth's rotation, deflects moving air and is directly proportional to wind velocity—faster winds experience greater deflection. Additionally, the force varies with latitude: it is absent at the equator and reaches its maximum at the poles. 

Understanding both dependencies is essential for questions on atmospheric dynamics and global wind patterns.

en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in assuming the Equator always gets more than 12 hours of sunlight and overlooking the Arctic Circle's 24-hour daylight. Many candidates misapply the solstice concept or confuse hemispheres, leading to incorrect elimination.
en.final_explanation:
On June 21 (Summer Solstice), the Sun is directly overhead at the Tropic of Cancer, giving it the longest day of the year—more than 12 hours of sunlight. 

The Arctic Circle experiences continuous daylight (24 hours). The Equator receives about 12 hours, not more, and the Tropic of Capricorn, being in the Southern Hemisphere's winter, gets less than 12 hours. 

Thus, only the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle experience more than 12 hours of sunlight on this date, making **option d correct.**

With reference to perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) that are used in making many consumer products, 
**Consider the following statements:**

1. PFAS are found to be widespread in drinking water, food and food packaging materials.

3. Persistent exposure to PFAS can lead to bioaccumulation in animal bodies.

**Which of the statements given above are correct?**

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: PFAS are found to be widespread in drinking water, food and food packaging materials.
statement_analysis.reason: PFAS contamination is commonly reported in water, food, and packaging due to their extensive industrial and consumer use.

statement_analysis.statement: PFAS are not easily degraded in the environment.
statement_analysis.reason: PFAS are known as 'forever chemicals' because they resist environmental degradation and persist for long periods.

statement_analysis.statement: Persistent exposure to PFAS can lead to bioaccumulation in animal bodies.
statement_analysis.reason: PFAS accumulate in living organisms over time, leading to bioaccumulation and potential health risks.

elimination_logic: All three statements are correct; any option omitting one is eliminated.
Scientific consensus supports the persistence, ubiquity, and bioaccumulation of PFAS.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in testing whether the candidate knows that all three statements are correct, as PFAS are often discussed for only one or two of these properties. The question checks for comprehensive understanding and not partial recall.
en.final_explanation:
**Option (d) **is correct because all three statements accurately describe PFAS: they are widespread in drinking water, food, and packaging; they are highly persistent in the environment; and they bioaccumulate in animal bodies with continued exposure. 

These properties make PFAS a significant environmental and public health concern, leading to global regulatory attention and research. Candidates should remember the 'forever chemical' nature and multi-pathway exposure risks of PFAS.

**Which one of the following is the correct description of “100 Million Farmers”?**

(a) It is a platform for accelerating the transition towards food and water systems that are net-zero (carbon), nature-positive and that aims to increase farmer resilience.

(b) It is an international alliance and a network of individuals and farming organisations interested in supporting and strengthening the development of organic animal husbandry.

(c) It is a digital platform fully integrated with service providers and built on blockchain that lets buyers, sellers and third parties trade fertilizers quickly and securely.

(d) It is a platform with the mission of encouraging farmers to form Farmer Producer Organisations or Agribusiness Consortiums, thus facilitating access to global open markets to sell their products.
elimination_logic: Options b and c describe unrelated platforms or initiatives, not matching the core purpose of '100 Million Farmers'.

en.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC uses scope-mismatch by offering options that sound plausible but subtly shift the focus away from the actual objectives of the '100 Million Farmers' initiative. The distractors use familiar agricultural development language to confuse candidates who do not recall the specific mandate.
en.final_explanation:
**Option (a) is correct** because the '100 Million Farmers' initiative is a global platform focused on transforming food and water systems to be net-zero (carbon), nature-positive, and resilient for farmers. 

The other options misrepresent the initiative by either focusing on unrelated aspects like organic animal husbandry, digital fertilizer trading, or FPO formation. 

The core concept is the transition towards sustainability and resilience in agriculture, which is explicitly stated in option (a).

en.display_text:
**Consider the following:**

1. Battery storage
2. Biomass generators
3. Fuel cells
4. Rooftop solar photovoltaic units

**How many of the above are considered "Distributed Energy Resources"?**

(a) Only one
(b) Only two
(c) Only three
(d) All four

statement_analysis.statement: Battery storage
statement_analysis.reason: Battery storage systems are classified as distributed energy resources as they can be deployed at or near the point of use.

statement_analysis.statement: Biomass generators
statement_analysis.reason: Biomass generators can be installed at distributed locations and supply power locally, qualifying as distributed energy resources.

statement_analysis.statement: Fuel cells
statement_analysis.reason: Fuel cells are modular, can be installed close to end-users, and are recognized as distributed energy resources.

statement_analysis.statement: Rooftop solar photovoltaic units
statement_analysis.reason: Rooftop solar PV units are a classic example of distributed energy resources, generating power at the consumer’s premises.

elimination_logic: Distributed energy resources include any small-scale units generating or storing power near the point of use.
Since all four options fit the definition, options a, b, and c are eliminated.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in testing whether the candidate recognizes that distributed energy resources encompass not only generation (like solar and biomass) but also storage (batteries) and advanced technologies (fuel cells). Many may overlook battery storage or fuel cells, thinking only of generation sources.
en.final_explanation:
All four listed technologies—battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells, and rooftop solar photovoltaic units—are considered distributed energy resources (DERs). 

DERs are small-scale units of local generation or storage connected to the grid at distribution level or behind the meter. They help decentralize energy production, improve grid resilience, and support renewable integration. 

Recognizing both generation and storage as DERs is essential for this question.

This unique, coevolved relationship is not found in Mahua, Sandalwood, or Silk cotton, which are pollinated by a variety of insects or animals. 

Thus, **option (a) is correct** as it directly addresses the exclusivity and coevolution described in the question.

en.display_text:
Which one of the following is synthesized in the human body that dilates blood vessels and increases blood flow?

(a) Nitric oxide

(b) Nitrous oxide

(c) Nitrogen dioxide

(d) Nitrogen pentoxide
elimination_logic: Options b, c, and d refer to nitrogen compounds not synthesized in the human body for vascular regulation.
Only option a matches the physiological role of vasodilation in humans.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in confusing similar-sounding nitrogen compounds. Candidates may mistakenly select nitrous oxide due to its medical use, but only nitric oxide is synthesized in the body for vasodilation.
en.final_explanation:
Nitric oxide (NO) is a gaseous signaling molecule produced by endothelial cells in the human body. It plays a crucial role in relaxing smooth muscle cells in blood vessels, leading to vasodilation and increased blood flow. 

The other options are either not synthesized in the body or have no physiological role in blood vessel regulation. Thus, option (a) is the correct answer.

Which one of the following is the exhaust pipe emission from Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles, powered by hydrogen?

(a) Hydrogen peroxide
(b) Hydronium
(c) Oxygen
(d) Water vapour
elimination_logic: Hydrogen peroxide and hydronium are not standard exhaust products of hydrogen fuel cells.
Oxygen is a reactant, not a product, in the fuel cell reaction.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap relies on confusing the role of oxygen in the fuel cell process and introducing uncommon chemical terms (hydrogen peroxide, hydronium) to distract candidates. Many may incorrectly assume oxygen is emitted, overlooking the actual chemical reaction.
en.final_explanation:
Hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicles generate electricity by combining hydrogen with oxygen from the air in a fuel cell. The only byproduct of this electrochemical reaction is water, which is released as water vapour through the exhaust. 

No harmful gases or other chemicals are emitted, making these vehicles environmentally friendly. Therefore, **the correct answer is water vapour.**

en.display_text:
Recently, the term **“Pumped-storage hydropower”** is actually and appropriately discussed in the context of which one of the following?

(a) Irrigation of terraced crop fields
(b) Lift irrigation of cereal crops
(c) Long duration energy storage
(d) Rainwater harvesting system
elimination_logic: Options a and b relate to irrigation, which is unrelated to the core function of pumped-storage hydropower.
Option d is about water collection, not energy storage.
Only option c correctly identifies the energy storage context.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in confusing the term 'pumped-storage' with agricultural or water management practices, leading candidates to select irrigation-related options. The correct context is energy storage, not water supply.
en.final_explanation:
Pumped-storage hydropower is a technology used to store large amounts of energy over long durations. It works by using surplus electricity to pump water from a lower reservoir to a higher one. 

When electricity demand rises, the stored water is released back down through turbines to generate power. This system is crucial for grid stability and integrating renewable energy sources. It is not related to irrigation or rainwater harvesting, making **option c the only correct answer.**

(a) Assisted reproductive technologies

en.final_explanation:
**Membrane bioreactors (MBRs)** integrate conventional biological treatment with membrane filtration, allowing for efficient removal of organic and inorganic contaminants from wastewater. 

This technology is widely adopted in municipal and industrial wastewater treatment plants due to its ability to produce high-quality effluent. The other options refer to fields where general bioreactors may be used, but the term 'membrane bioreactor' is specifically associated with wastewater treatment technologies.

en.display_text:
With reference to the Indian economy, "Collateral Borrowing and Lending Obligations" are the instruments of:

(a) Bond market
(b) Forex market
(c) Money market
(d) Stock market
elimination_logic: CBLO is a short-term instrument, so options related to long-term or equity markets (a, d) can be eliminated.
CBLO is not related to currency exchange, eliminating option b.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap is conceptual-misapplication: candidates may confuse CBLO with instruments of bond or stock markets due to the term 'collateral' or 'obligation', or with forex due to 'borrowing/lending'. Only those with clear money market knowledge will answer correctly.
en.final_explanation:
Collateral Borrowing and Lending Obligations (CBLO) are instruments of the money market in India. They facilitate short-term borrowing and lending operations, primarily among banks, financial institutions, and other eligible entities, using government securities as collateral. 

CBLO provides liquidity management and is regulated by the Clearing Corporation of India Ltd (CCIL). It is not related to bond, forex, or stock markets, which deal with different types of financial instruments.

en.display_text:
The **"Total fertility rate"** in an economy is defined as:

(a) the number of children born per 1000 people in the population in a year.

(b) the number of children born to a couple in their lifetime in a given population.

(c) the birth rate minus death rate.

(d) the average number of live births a woman would have by the end of her child-bearing age.
elimination_logic: Option a is eliminated as it defines crude birth rate, not total fertility rate.
Option b is eliminated because it focuses on a couple, not the average per woman.
Option c is eliminated as it refers to natural increase, not fertility rate.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC tests the ability to distinguish between similar demographic terms. The trap lies in confusing total fertility rate with crude birth rate, natural increase, or focusing on couples instead of individual women.
en.final_explanation:
**Option d is correct** because the total fertility rate (TFR) specifically measures the average number of live births a woman would have by the end of her reproductive years, assuming current age-specific fertility rates remain constant. 

This indicator is crucial for understanding population growth trends and is distinct from crude birth rate or natural increase, which measure different aspects of population dynamics. TFR is a standard demographic measure used globally.

किसी अर्थव्यवस्था में **"कुल प्रजनन दर"** को परिभाषित किया जाता है:

(a) प्रति वर्ष प्रति 1000 जनसंख्या में जन्मे बच्चों की संख्या।

(b) किसी दिए गए जनसंख्या में एक दंपति के जीवनकाल में जन्मे बच्चों की संख्या।

(c) जन्म दर में से मृत्यु दर को घटाना।

(d) एक महिला द्वारा उसके प्रजनन काल के अंत तक होने वाले औसत जीवित जन्मों की संख्या।
elimination_logic: विकल्प a को इसलिए खारिज किया गया क्योंकि यह कुल प्रजनन दर नहीं, बल्कि सकल जन्म दर को परिभाषित करता है।
विकल्प b को इसलिए खारिज किया गया क्योंकि यह एक दंपति पर केंद्रित है, न कि प्रति महिला औसत पर।
विकल्प c को इसलिए खारिज किया गया क्योंकि यह प्राकृतिक वृद्धि को संदर्भित करता है, न कि प्रजनन दर को।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC समान जनसांख्यिकीय शब्दों के बीच अंतर करने की क्षमता का परीक्षण करता है। जाल इस बात में है कि कुल प्रजनन दर को सकल जन्म दर, प्राकृतिक वृद्धि या दंपतियों पर ध्यान केंद्रित करने के साथ भ्रमित कर दिया जाए, जबकि यह व्यक्तिगत महिलाओं पर आधारित होता है।
hi.final_explanation:
**विकल्प d सही है** क्योंकि कुल प्रजनन दर (TFR) विशेष रूप से उस औसत संख्या को मापती है जो एक महिला अपने प्रजनन काल के अंत तक जीवित बच्चों के रूप में जन्म देगी, यदि वर्तमान आयु-विशिष्ट प्रजनन दर स्थिर बनी रहती है।

यह संकेतक जनसंख्या वृद्धि के रुझानों को समझने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है और यह सकल जन्म दर या प्राकृतिक वृद्धि से भिन्न है, जो जनसंख्या गतिशीलता के विभिन्न पहलुओं को मापते हैं। TFR एक मानक जनसांख्यिकीय माप है जो विश्व स्तर पर उपयोग किया जाता है।

en.final_explanation:

With reference to the rule/rules imposed by the Reserve Bank of India while treating foreign banks, consider the following statements:

statement_analysis.statement: There is no minimum capital requirement for wholly owned banking subsidiaries in India.
statement_analysis.reason: RBI mandates a minimum capital requirement for wholly owned banking subsidiaries of foreign banks in India.

statement_analysis.statement: For wholly owned banking subsidiaries in India, at least 50% of the board members should be Indian nationals.
statement_analysis.reason: RBI does not require at least 50% of the board members to be Indian nationals for such subsidiaries.

elimination_logic: Statement 1 is incorrect; eliminate options containing only 1.
Statement 2 is incorrect; eliminate options containing only 2.
Both statements are incorrect; only option d remains.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC uses partial-truth and extreme-qualifier traps here. Both statements appear plausible but use absolute language ('no minimum', 'at least 50%'), which is not supported by RBI regulations. Candidates may be misled by overgeneralization or lack of precise recall.
en.final_explanation:
**Option d is correct** because both statements are factually incorrect. The RBI requires a minimum capital for wholly owned subsidiaries of foreign banks in India, **contrary to statement 1. **

**Statement 2 is also incorrect** as there is no RBI mandate requiring at least 50% of board members to be Indian nationals. 

**Candidates must be careful with absolute statements.**

en.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC tests awareness of the statutory 2% minimum CSR spending requirement. The trap lies in the second statement, which subtly contradicts a well-known legal provision, tempting candidates to overlook this detail.
en.final_explanation:
**Option (a) is correct** because CSR rules in India clearly state that any expenditure benefiting only the company or its employees is not considered a CSR activity.

**Consider the following statements in respect of the digital rupee:**

1. It is a sovereign currency issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in alignment with its monetary policy.

2. It appears as a liability on the RBI’s balance sheet.

3. It is insured against inflation by its very design.

4. It is freely convertible against commercial bank money and cash.

**Which of the statements given above are correct?**
(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 2 and 4 only
(d) 1, 2 and 4

statement_analysis.statement: It is a sovereign currency issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in alignment with its monetary policy.
statement_analysis.reason: The digital rupee is a central bank digital currency (CBDC) issued by RBI and is a sovereign liability, aligned with RBI’s monetary policy.

statement_analysis.statement: It appears as a liability on the RBI’s balance sheet.
statement_analysis.reason: CBDC, like physical currency, is a liability of the RBI and is recorded as such on its balance sheet.

statement_analysis.statement: It is insured against inflation by its very design.
statement_analysis.reason: No currency, including the digital rupee, is inherently protected against inflation by design; its value can erode with inflation.

statement_analysis.statement: It is freely convertible against commercial bank money and cash.
statement_analysis.reason: Digital rupee is designed to be freely convertible with commercial bank deposits and physical cash at par.

elimination_logic: Statement 3 is factually incorrect; any option including it (b) must be eliminated.
Statement 1 is correct; options excluding it (c) are invalid.
Statement 4 is correct; options excluding it (a) are incomplete.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in statement 3, which superficially sounds plausible but is conceptually flawed. Many candidates may wrongly assume that a digital currency is inflation-proof by design, leading to incorrect selection. The question tests nuanced understanding of central bank money and monetary policy.
en.final_explanation:
**Option d is correct** because statements 1, 2, and 4 accurately describe the digital rupee: it is a sovereign currency issued by RBI, appears as a liability on RBI’s balance sheet, and is freely convertible with commercial bank money and cash. 

**Statement 3 is incorrect**, as no currency is inherently protected against inflation by its design. This question tests knowledge of CBDC fundamentals and the distinction between currency design and macroeconomic factors like inflation.

**With reference to revenue collection by Cornwallis, consider the following statements:**

1. Under the Ryotwari Settlement of revenue collection, the peasants were exempted from revenue payment in case of bad harvests or natural calamities.

2. Under the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, if the Zamindar failed to pay his revenues to the state on or before the fixed date, he would be removed from his Zamindari.

(b) 2 only

statement_analysis.statement: Under the Ryotwari Settlement of revenue collection, the peasants were exempted from revenue payment in case of bad harvests or natural calamities.
statement_analysis.reason: Ryotwari Settlement was not introduced by Cornwallis and did not provide automatic exemption for peasants during bad harvests or calamities.

statement_analysis.statement: Under the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, if the Zamindar failed to pay his revenues to the state on or before the fixed date, he would be removed from his Zamindari.
statement_analysis.reason: Permanent Settlement stipulated that failure to pay revenue by the due date led to the Zamindar’s removal and auction of his estate.

elimination_logic: Statement 1 is incorrect, so options containing '1' (a, c) are eliminated.
Statement 2 is correct, so option (d) is eliminated.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC tests knowledge of who introduced which revenue system and the specific provisions of each. The trap is in associating Ryotwari with Cornwallis and assuming leniency for peasants, while the real factual detail lies in the strictness of Permanent Settlement.
en.final_explanation:
• The Ryotwari Settlement was not introduced by Cornwallis and did not guarantee exemption from revenue during bad harvests; such exemptions were rare and not a formal provision.
• Under the Permanent Settlement (introduced by Cornwallis in Bengal), Zamindars were required to pay a fixed revenue by a certain date. Failure to do so resulted in their removal and auction of their estates.
• **Therefore, only Statement 2 is correct**, making option (b) the right answer.

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements:

1. There are no parables in Upanishads.

2. Upanishads were composed earlier than the Puranas.

**Which of the statements given above is/are correct?**

(a) 1 only
(b) 2 only
(c) Both 1 and 2
(d) Neither 1 nor 2

statement_analysis.statement: There are no parables in Upanishads.
statement_analysis.reason: Upanishads contain several parables and stories to explain philosophical ideas, such as the story of Nachiketa in the Katha Upanishad.

statement_analysis.statement: Upanishads were composed earlier than the Puranas.
statement_analysis.reason: Upanishads are part of Vedic literature (circa 800–500 BCE), while Puranas were composed much later, mostly after the Vedic period.

elimination_logic: Statement 1 is incorrect; any option including it as correct is eliminated.
Only Statement 2 is correct; thus, only option b remains.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in the extreme qualifier 'no parables' in Statement 1, which may mislead candidates who overlook the narrative content of Upanishads. The chronology aspect in Statement 2 tests basic historical sequencing.
en.final_explanation:
**Option b is correct** because the Upanishads, which are part of the later Vedic literature, were composed much earlier than the Puranas. 

The Upanishads use parables and stories to convey philosophical teachings, **making Statement 1 incorrect. **

**Statement 2 is correct** as the Puranas were compiled in the post-Vedic period, centuries after the Upanishads. Thus, only Statement 2 holds true.

en.display_text:
**Consider the following statements:**
1. India is a member of the International Grains Council.
2. A country needs to be a member of the International Grains Council for exporting or importing rice and wheat.

**Which of the statements given above is/are correct?**
(a) 1 only
(b) 2 only
(c) Both 1 and 2
(d) Neither 1 nor 2

statement_analysis.statement: India is a member of the International Grains Council.
statement_analysis.reason: India is officially listed as a member of the International Grains Council (IGC), an intergovernmental organization focused on grains trade.

statement_analysis.statement: A country needs to be a member of the International Grains Council for exporting or importing rice and wheat.
statement_analysis.reason: Membership of the IGC is not a mandatory requirement for a country to export or import rice and wheat; non-members can also trade these grains.

elimination_logic: Since Statement 2 is incorrect, options containing it as correct (b and c) are eliminated.
Since Statement 1 is correct, option d is eliminated.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in the over-generalization of international membership requirements. Statement 2 uses an absolute qualifier, making candidates assume international bodies control all trade, which is not the case. This tests awareness of actual trade protocols.
en.final_explanation:
**Option (a) is correct **because India is indeed a member of the International Grains Council, an intergovernmental forum for cooperation in grains trade. 

However, membership in the IGC is not a prerequisite for any country to export or import rice and wheat. Many countries trade these commodities without being IGC members. 

The question tests knowledge of international trade protocols and India's participation in global commodity councils.

**With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:**

statement_analysis.statement: It provided for the establishment of an All India Federation based on the union of the British Indian Provinces and Princely States.

statement_analysis.statement: Defence and Foreign Affairs were kept under the control of the federal legislature.
statement_analysis.reason: Defence and Foreign Affairs were reserved subjects under the direct control of the Governor-General, not the federal legislature.

elimination_logic: Statement 2 is factually incorrect, so options containing it (b and c) must be eliminated.
Option d is eliminated as Statement 1 is correct.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC tests whether candidates recall that Defence and Foreign Affairs remained reserved subjects under the Governor-General, not the federal legislature. The trap is in assuming all powers were federated.
en.final_explanation:
**Option (a) is correct** because the Government of India Act, 1935, indeed provided for an All India Federation comprising British Indian Provinces and Princely States. 

However, Defence and Foreign Affairs were not under the federal legislature; they were reserved subjects under the direct control of the Governor-General. 

This distinction is crucial for understanding the limited nature of federal autonomy under the Act.

**Which of the following statements are correct in respect of a Money Bill in the Parliament?**

1. Article 109 mentions special procedure in respect of Money Bills.

2. A Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Council of States.

3. The Rajya Sabha can either approve the Bill or suggest changes but cannot reject it.

4. Amendments to a Money Bill suggested by the Rajya Sabha have to be accepted by the Lok Sabha.

**Select the answer using the code given below:**
(a) 1 and 2 only

(b) 2 and 3 only

(c) 1, 2 and 3

(d) 1, 3 and 4

statement_analysis.statement: Article 109 mentions special procedure in respect of Money Bills.
statement_analysis.reason: Article 109 of the Constitution specifically deals with the special procedure for Money Bills in Parliament.

statement_analysis.statement: A Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Council of States.
statement_analysis.reason: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, not in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

statement_analysis.statement: The Rajya Sabha can either approve the Bill or suggest changes but cannot reject it.
statement_analysis.reason: Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only recommend changes, which Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

statement_analysis.statement: Amendments to a Money Bill suggested by the Rajya Sabha have to be accepted by the Lok Sabha.
statement_analysis.reason: Lok Sabha is not bound to accept any amendments suggested by Rajya Sabha on a Money Bill.

elimination_logic: Statement 4 is incorrect, so options containing it (d) are eliminated.
Statement 1 is correct, so options omitting it (b) are eliminated.
Statement 3 is correct, so options omitting it (a) are eliminated.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in the subtle difference between Rajya Sabha's power to suggest amendments and Lok Sabha's discretion to accept or reject them. Statement 4 is a partial-truth trap, as it misleads by implying Lok Sabha must accept amendments.
en.final_explanation:
**Option c is correct **because statements 1, 2, and 3 accurately reflect the constitutional provisions regarding Money Bills. 

Article 109 lays down the special procedure, restricting introduction to Lok Sabha only. Rajya Sabha's role is limited to making recommendations, which Lok Sabha may accept or reject. 

**Statement 4 is incorrect** because Lok Sabha is not bound to accept Rajya Sabha's suggestions. Understanding these distinctions is crucial for interpreting the legislative process for Money Bills.

The North Eastern Council (NEC) was established by the North Eastern Council Act, 1971. Subsequent to the amendment of NEC Act in 2002, the Council comprises which of the following members?

3. Three Members to be nominated by the President of India
4. The Home Minister of India

**Select the correct answer using the code given below:**

statement_analysis.statement: Chief Minister of the Constituent State

statement_analysis.reason: The amended Act provides for three members nominated by the President.

en.final_explanation:

The Union Minister for Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) serves as the ex-officio Chairman, not the Home Minister.

concepts_used: Right to Privacy is a part of Article 21.
Supreme Court judgments have expanded Article 21 to include various rights.

en.display_text:
**Under which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India has the Supreme Court of India placed the Right to Privacy?**

(a) Article 15

(b) Article 16

(c) Article 19

(d) Article 21
elimination_logic: Articles 15 and 16 are about equality and non-discrimination, not privacy.
Article 19 covers freedoms, but privacy is not directly placed here by the Supreme Court.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in confusing the scope of fundamental rights. Options a, b, and c are all fundamental rights articles, which may mislead candidates into associating privacy with general freedoms or equality, rather than the specific protection of life and personal liberty under Article 21.
en.final_explanation:
The Supreme Court of India, in the landmark Puttaswamy judgment (2017), declared that the Right to Privacy is a fundamental right protected under Article 21 of the Constitution. 

Article 21 ensures the protection of life and personal liberty, and the Court has interpreted this to include privacy as an essential aspect. Options a, b, and c do not provide the constitutional basis for the Right to Privacy as recognized by the Supreme Court. 

**Thus, option d is the correct answer.**

अनुच्छेद 21 जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता की सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करता है, और न्यायालय ने इसे निजता को एक आवश्यक पहलू मानते हुए व्याख्यायित किया है। विकल्प a, b, और c सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा मान्यता प्राप्त निजता के अधिकार के लिए संवैधानिक आधार प्रदान नहीं करते।

en.display_text:
**A Writ of Prohibition is an order issued by the Supreme Court or High Courts to:**

(a) a government officer prohibiting him from taking a particular action.
(b) the Parliament/Legislative Assembly to pass a law on Prohibition.
(c) the lower court prohibiting continuation of proceedings in a case.
(d) the Government prohibiting it from following an unconstitutional policy.
elimination_logic: Options a and d misapply the writ to executive actions, which is incorrect.
Option b wrongly assigns the writ to legislative functions, which courts cannot direct.
Only option c correctly identifies the judicial context and target of the writ.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in confusing the target of the writ. Many candidates may think writs can be issued to government officers or the legislature, but Prohibition specifically applies to lower courts or tribunals, not executive or legislative bodies.
en.final_explanation:
The Writ of Prohibition is a judicial remedy issued by the Supreme Court or High Courts to lower courts or tribunals, directing them to stop proceedings in cases where they are acting outside their jurisdiction. It ensures that subordinate courts do not exceed their legal authority. 

This writ cannot be issued to executive or legislative bodies, making option c the only correct answer. Understanding the specific application and target of each constitutional writ is essential for accurate answer selection.

यह आदेश कार्यकारी या विधायी निकायों को जारी नहीं किया जा सकता, इसलिए विकल्प (c) ही एकमात्र सही उत्तर है। प्रत्येक संवैधानिक आदेश के विशिष्ट प्रयोग और लक्ष्य को समझना सही उत्तर चयन के लिए आवश्यक है।

**With reference to the Union Budget, consider the following statements:**

1. The Union Finance Minister, on behalf of the Prime Minister, lays the Annual Financial Statement before both Houses of Parliament.

(b) 2 only

(d) Neither 1 nor 2

statement_analysis.statement: The Union Finance Minister, on behalf of the Prime Minister, lays the Annual Financial Statement before both Houses of Parliament.
statement_analysis.reason: The Finance Minister presents the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) in Parliament, acting on behalf of the government led by the Prime Minister.

statement_analysis.statement: At the Union level, no demand for a grant can be made except on the recommendation of the President of India.
statement_analysis.reason: Article 113(3) of the Constitution mandates that no demand for a grant can be made except on the President's recommendation.

elimination_logic: Options a and b can be eliminated as both statements are correct.
Option d can be eliminated as neither statement is incorrect.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The question tests detailed knowledge of budgetary procedure and constitutional provisions. The trap lies in the subtle wording of statement 1, which may confuse candidates about the Finance Minister's role vis-à-vis the Prime Minister, and in the technical requirement of the President's recommendation for grants.
en.final_explanation:
**Both statements are correct**. 

The Finance Minister, representing the government headed by the Prime Minister, lays the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) before both Houses of Parliament. 

Additionally, Article 113(3) of the Constitution specifies that no demand for a grant can be made except on the President's recommendation. 

These are foundational aspects of the Union Budget process,** making option (c) the correct answer.**

**Statement-I:**
Sumed pipeline is a strategic route for Persian Gulf oil and natural gas shipments to Europe.

Sumed pipeline connects the Red Sea with the Mediterranean Sea.

**Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?**

(a) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I

(b) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I

statement_analysis.statement: Sumed pipeline is a strategic route for Persian Gulf oil and natural gas shipments to Europe.

elimination_logic: Options c and d are eliminated because both statements are correct.

en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in testing whether candidates recognize that Statement-II is not just correct, but also the direct reason for Statement-I. Many may overlook the causal linkage and choose option (b) instead of (a).

**Option (a) is correct** because both statements are factually accurate and Statement-II directly explains Statement-I. 

The Sumed pipeline connects the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea, allowing oil from the Persian Gulf to bypass the Suez Canal and reach Europe efficiently.

According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which one of the following is the largest source of sulphur dioxide emissions?

en.upsc_trap_explanation: The question uses similar-sounding industrial sources to confuse candidates. The trap lies in overestimating the impact of metal extraction or transport sources, while the largest contributor is power generation, which is often overlooked due to its ubiquity.
en.final_explanation:
Power plants using fossil fuels, particularly coal, are the largest source of sulphur dioxide emissions globally and as per the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). 

These plants burn massive quantities of fossil fuels, releasing significant amounts of SO2 into the atmosphere. Other sources like locomotives, ships, and metal extraction contribute to emissions but at a much smaller scale. **Thus, option (d) is correct.**

While any resolution for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is under consideration:

statement_analysis.statement: He/She shall not preside.
statement_analysis.reason: Article 96(1) of the Constitution states the Speaker shall not preside while a resolution for removal is under consideration.

statement_analysis.statement: He/She shall not have the right to speak.
statement_analysis.reason: The Speaker can speak and take part in proceedings when a resolution for removal is under consideration.

statement_analysis.statement: He/She shall not be entitled to vote on the resolution in the first instance.
statement_analysis.reason: The Speaker can vote as an ordinary member; the restriction is only on presiding, not on voting.

elimination_logic: Any option including Statement 2 is eliminated as the Speaker retains the right to speak.
Any option including Statement 3 is eliminated as the Speaker can vote as a member.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC tests nuanced understanding of constitutional provisions regarding the Speaker’s rights during removal proceedings. The trap lies in assuming the Speaker loses all participatory rights, when only the right to preside is suspended.
en.final_explanation:
**Statement 1 is correct** as per Article 96(1): the Speaker shall not preside while a removal resolution is under consideration. 

However, the Speaker can participate in the proceedings, including speaking and voting as an ordinary member.** Statements 2 and 3 are thus incorrect**. 

This question tests precise knowledge of constitutional procedure for the removal of the Speaker. Only option (a) aligns with the constitutional text and official answer key.

**With reference to the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements:**

1. A bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its dissolution.

2. A bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

3. A bill in regard to which the President of India notified his/her intention to summon the Houses to a joint sitting lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

**Which of the statements given above is/are correct?**
(a) 1 only
(b) 1 and 2
(c) 2 and 3
(d) 3 only

statement_analysis.statement: A bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its dissolution.
statement_analysis.reason: Any bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses upon its dissolution as per Article 107(5) of the Constitution.

statement_analysis.statement: A bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
statement_analysis.reason: If the Lok Sabha is dissolved, any bill passed by it but pending in the Rajya Sabha also lapses.

statement_analysis.statement: A bill in regard to which the President of India notified his/her intention to summon the Houses to a joint sitting lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
statement_analysis.reason: Such a bill does not lapse; it is specifically saved under Article 108(5) even if the Lok Sabha is dissolved.

elimination_logic: Statement 3 is incorrect; eliminate options containing it.
Option a is incomplete as it ignores correct statement 2.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The trap lies in the nuanced difference between bills pending in different stages and the special case of joint sitting notification. Many candidates wrongly assume all bills lapse on dissolution, missing the constitutional exception for joint sitting.
en.final_explanation:
**Statements 1 and 2 are correct** as per Articles 107(5) and 108(5) of the Constitution: bills pending in the Lok Sabha or passed by Lok Sabha but pending in Rajya Sabha lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha. 

However, a bill for which the President has notified a joint sitting does not lapse, as it is specifically protected by the Constitution. Therefore, option b is correct, as it includes only the accurate statements.

en.display_text:
**With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements:**

1. Prorogation of a House by the President of India does not require the advice of the Council of Ministers.

2. Prorogation of a House is generally done after the House is adjourned sine die, but there is no bar to the President of India proroguing the House which is in session.

3. Dissolution of the Lok Sabha is done by the President of India who, save in exceptional circumstances, does so on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

**Which of the statements given above is/are correct?**
(a) 1 only
(b) 1 and 2
(c) 2 and 3
(d) 3 only

statement_analysis.statement: Prorogation of a House by the President of India does not require the advice of the Council of Ministers.
statement_analysis.reason: The President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers for prorogation, as per established constitutional practice.

statement_analysis.statement: Prorogation of a House is generally done after the House is adjourned sine die, but there is no bar to the President of India proroguing the House which is in session.
statement_analysis.reason: Prorogation usually follows adjournment sine die, but the President can prorogue the House even when it is in session.

statement_analysis.statement: Dissolution of the Lok Sabha is done by the President of India who, save in exceptional circumstances, does so on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
statement_analysis.reason: The President dissolves the Lok Sabha on the advice of the Council of Ministers, except in rare situations.

elimination_logic: Statement 1 is incorrect; eliminate options a and b.
Option d ignores the correctness of Statement 2; eliminate d.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC tests nuanced understanding of constitutional procedures regarding prorogation and dissolution. The trap lies in the subtle difference between the President's formal powers and the requirement to act on ministerial advice, especially for prorogation.
en.final_explanation:
**Option c is correct** because both Statements 2 and 3 accurately reflect constitutional practice. The President generally prorogues a House after adjournment sine die, but can do so even when the House is in session. 

Dissolution of the Lok Sabha is carried out by the President, almost always on the advice of the Council of Ministers, except in rare, exceptional circumstances. 

**Statement 1 is incorrect** because the President does require ministerial advice for prorogation. Understanding these distinctions is essential for mastering parliamentary procedures.

en.upsc_trap_explanation: The question uses an extreme qualifier in Statement 1 ('100% funding'), which may prompt candidates to doubt its accuracy. Additionally, the transliteration initiative in Statement 3 may be unfamiliar, leading to hesitation. The trap lies in testing detailed knowledge of scheme components and funding patterns.
en.final_explanation:
**Option (d) is correct** because all three statements accurately reflect the features of the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme. 

The scheme is centrally funded, includes digitization of cadastral maps, and has initiated transliteration of land records into all languages recognized by the Constitution. 

This comprehensive approach aims to modernize land records, improve transparency, and enhance accessibility for citizens across linguistic backgrounds.

1. This scheme guarantees a minimum package of antenatal care services to women in their second and third trimesters of pregnancy and six months post-delivery health care service in any government health facility.

2. Under this scheme, private sector health care providers of certain specialties can volunteer to provide services at nearby government health facilities.

**Which of the statements given above is/are correct?**
(a) 1 only
(b) 2 only
(c) Both 1 and 2
(d) Neither 1 nor 2

statement_analysis.statement: This scheme guarantees a minimum package of antenatal care services to women in their second and third trimesters of pregnancy and six months post-delivery health care service in any government health facility.
statement_analysis.reason: The scheme covers antenatal care for women in their second and third trimesters, but does not guarantee six months post-delivery health care.

statement_analysis.statement: Under this scheme, private sector health care providers of certain specialties can volunteer to provide services at nearby government health facilities.
statement_analysis.reason: The scheme allows private sector specialists to volunteer and provide services at government health facilities.

elimination_logic: Statement 1 is incorrect due to the inclusion of post-delivery care, so options containing only Statement 1 or both are eliminated.
Statement 2 is correct, so options excluding it are eliminated.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The question uses a partial-truth trap by embedding an incorrect extension (six months post-delivery care) into Statement 1, which may mislead candidates who recall only the antenatal care aspect. Statement 2 tests awareness of private sector involvement.
en.final_explanation:
**Option (b) is correct** because the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan ensures antenatal care for pregnant women in their second and third trimesters, but does not guarantee six months post-delivery care as stated in Statement 1. 

Statement 2 is correct, as the scheme explicitly allows private sector specialists to volunteer and provide services at government health facilities. 

This public-private partnership approach is a key feature of the scheme, aiming to improve maternal health outcomes by leveraging additional expertise.

hi.display_text:
**‘प्रधान मंत्री सुरक्षित मातृत्व अभियान’ के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:**

1. यह योजना गर्भावस्था के दूसरे और तीसरे त्रैमास में महिलाओं को न्यूनतम प्रसवपूर्व देखभाल सेवाओं का पैकेज और प्रसव के बाद छह महीने तक किसी भी सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सुविधा में स्वास्थ्य सेवा की गारंटी देती है।

2. इस योजना के तहत, निजी क्षेत्र के कुछ विशेष क्षेत्रों के स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदाता निकटवर्ती सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सुविधाओं में स्वयंसेवक के रूप में सेवाएँ प्रदान कर सकते हैं।

**उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?**
(a) केवल 1
(b) केवल 2
(c) 1 और 2 दोनों
(d) न तो 1, न ही 2

statement_analysis.statement: यह योजना गर्भावस्था के दूसरे और तीसरे त्रैमास में महिलाओं को न्यूनतम प्रसवपूर्व देखभाल सेवाओं का पैकेज और प्रसव के बाद छह महीने तक किसी भी सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सुविधा में स्वास्थ्य सेवा की गारंटी देती है।
statement_analysis.reason: यह योजना गर्भावस्था के दूसरे और तीसरे त्रैमास में प्रसवपूर्व देखभाल प्रदान करती है, लेकिन प्रसव के बाद छह महीने तक की स्वास्थ्य सेवा की गारंटी नहीं देती।

statement_analysis.statement: इस योजना के तहत, निजी क्षेत्र के कुछ विशेष क्षेत्रों के स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदाता निकटवर्ती सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सुविधाओं में स्वयंसेवक के रूप में सेवाएँ प्रदान कर सकते हैं।
statement_analysis.reason: यह योजना निजी क्षेत्र के विशेषज्ञों को स्वयंसेवक के रूप में सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सुविधाओं में सेवाएँ प्रदान करने की अनुमति देती है।

elimination_logic: कथन 1 प्रसव के बाद देखभाल शामिल करने के कारण गलत है, अतः केवल कथन 1 या दोनों वाले विकल्प हटा दिए जाते हैं।
कथन 2 सही है, इसलिए इसे छोड़ने वाले विकल्प हटा दिए जाते हैं।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: यह प्रश्न आंशिक सत्य के जाल का उपयोग करता है, जिसमें कथन 1 में गलत विस्तार (प्रसव के बाद छह महीने की देखभाल) शामिल है, जो केवल प्रसवपूर्व देखभाल को याद रखने वाले उम्मीदवारों को भ्रमित कर सकता है। कथन 2 निजी क्षेत्र की भागीदारी की जानकारी परखता है।
hi.final_explanation:
**विकल्प (b) सही है** क्योंकि प्रधानमंत्री सुरक्षित मातृत्व अभियान गर्भवती महिलाओं को उनके दूसरे और तीसरे त्रैमास में प्रसवपूर्व देखभाल सुनिश्चित करता है, लेकिन कथन 1 में बताए अनुसार प्रसव के बाद छह महीने की देखभाल की गारंटी नहीं देता।

कथन 2 सही है, क्योंकि यह योजना स्पष्ट रूप से निजी क्षेत्र के विशेषज्ञों को स्वयंसेवक के रूप में सरकारी स्वास्थ्य सुविधाओं में सेवाएँ प्रदान करने की अनुमति देती है।

यह सार्वजनिक-निजी भागीदारी दृष्टिकोण योजना की एक प्रमुख विशेषता है, जिसका उद्देश्य अतिरिक्त विशेषज्ञता का उपयोग कर मातृ स्वास्थ्य परिणामों में सुधार करना है।

en.display_text:
**With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) Yojana, consider the following statements:**

1. The entry age group for enrolment in the scheme is 21 to 40 years.

2. Age-specific contribution shall be made by the beneficiary.

3. Each subscriber under the scheme shall receive a minimum pension of INR 3,000 per month after attaining the age of 60 years.

4. Family pension is applicable to the spouse and unmarried daughters.

**Which of the statements given above is/are correct?**

(a) 1, 3 and 4

(b) 2 and 3 only

(c) 2 only

(d) 1, 2 and 4

statement_analysis.statement: The entry age group for enrolment in the scheme is 21 to 40 years.
statement_analysis.reason: The correct entry age for PM-SYM is 18 to 40 years, not 21 to 40 years.

statement_analysis.statement: Age-specific contribution shall be made by the beneficiary.
statement_analysis.reason: Beneficiaries contribute monthly based on their entry age as per the scheme guidelines.

statement_analysis.statement: Each subscriber under the scheme shall receive a minimum pension of 3,000 per month after attaining the age of 60 years.
statement_analysis.reason: The scheme guarantees a minimum monthly pension of ₹3,000 after 60 years of age.

statement_analysis.statement: Family pension is applicable to the spouse and unmarried daughters.
statement_analysis.reason: Family pension is only applicable to the spouse, not to unmarried daughters.

elimination_logic: Statement 1 is factually incorrect; eliminate options containing 1.
Statement 4 is incorrect; eliminate options containing 4.
Only options with statements 2 and 3 remain valid.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC uses partial-truth traps by tweaking age limits and family pension eligibility, both of which are easy to misremember. Candidates may also assume unmarried daughters are covered, leading to incorrect selection.
en.final_explanation:
**Option (b) is correct** because only statements 2 and 3 accurately reflect the provisions of the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan Yojana. 

The scheme requires age-specific contributions from beneficiaries and guarantees a minimum pension of ₹3,000 per month after 60 years of age. 

The entry age is 18–40 years (not 21–40), and family pension is provided only to the spouse, not to unmarried daughters. Remembering these specifics is crucial for accurate answer selection.

hi.display_text:
**प्रधान मंत्री श्रम योगी मान-धन (PM-SYM) योजना के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:**

1. योजना में नामांकन के लिए प्रवेश आयु वर्ग 21 से 40 वर्ष है।

2. लाभार्थी द्वारा आयु-विशिष्ट योगदान किया जाएगा।

3. योजना के तहत प्रत्येक सदस्य को 60 वर्ष की आयु प्राप्त करने के बाद न्यूनतम मासिक पेंशन ₹3,000 प्राप्त होगी।

4. पारिवारिक पेंशन पति/पत्नी और अविवाहित बेटियों दोनों पर लागू होती है।

**उपरोक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?**

(a) 1, 3 और 4

(b) केवल 2 और 3

(c) केवल 2

(d) 1, 2 और 4

statement_analysis.statement: योजना में नामांकन के लिए प्रवेश आयु वर्ग 21 से 40 वर्ष है।
statement_analysis.reason: PM-SYM के लिए सही प्रवेश आयु 18 से 40 वर्ष है, न कि 21 से 40 वर्ष।

statement_analysis.statement: लाभार्थी द्वारा आयु-विशिष्ट योगदान किया जाएगा।
statement_analysis.reason: लाभार्थी योजना के निर्देशानुसार अपनी प्रवेश आयु के आधार पर मासिक योगदान करते हैं।

statement_analysis.statement: योजना के तहत प्रत्येक सदस्य को 60 वर्ष की आयु प्राप्त करने के बाद न्यूनतम मासिक पेंशन ₹3,000 प्राप्त होगी।
statement_analysis.reason: योजना 60 वर्ष की आयु के बाद न्यूनतम ₹3,000 मासिक पेंशन की गारंटी देती है।

statement_analysis.statement: पारिवारिक पेंशन पति/पत्नी और अविवाहित बेटियों दोनों पर लागू होती है।
statement_analysis.reason: पारिवारिक पेंशन केवल पति/पत्नी को ही लागू होती है, अविवाहित बेटियों को नहीं।

elimination_logic: कथन 1 तथ्यात्मक रूप से गलत है; जिन विकल्पों में 1 है उन्हें हटा दें।
कथन 4 गलत है; जिन विकल्पों में 4 है उन्हें हटा दें।
केवल कथन 2 और 3 वाले विकल्प मान्य रह जाते हैं।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: UPSC आंशिक सत्य के जाल का उपयोग करता है, जैसे आयु सीमा और पारिवारिक पेंशन पात्रता में बदलाव, जिन्हें याद रखना आसान नहीं होता। उम्मीदवार यह भी मान सकते हैं कि अविवाहित बेटियाँ भी शामिल हैं, जिससे गलत विकल्प चुनने की संभावना बढ़ जाती है।
hi.final_explanation:
**विकल्प (b) सही है** क्योंकि केवल कथन 2 और 3 ही प्रधान मंत्री श्रम योगी मान-धन योजना के प्रावधानों को सही रूप में दर्शाते हैं।

यह योजना लाभार्थियों से आयु-विशिष्ट योगदान की मांग करती है और 60 वर्ष की आयु के बाद न्यूनतम ₹3,000 मासिक पेंशन की गारंटी देती है।

प्रवेश आयु 18–40 वर्ष है (21–40 नहीं), और पारिवारिक पेंशन केवल पति/पत्नी को ही दी जाती है, अविवाहित बेटियों को नहीं। इन विशिष्टताओं को याद रखना सही उत्तर चयन के लिए आवश्यक है।
